newsitem.title: USA: USDA - Canada pledges to limit wheat to U.S.
newsitem.headline: USDA - Canada pledges to limit wheat to U.S.

text.p: Canada has agreed to limit its wheat and barley exports to the United States this year to no more than 1.5 million tonnes, a senior U.S. Agriculture Department official said Thursday.

Testifying before a House Agriculture subcommittee, August Schumacher, head of USDA's Foreign Agricultural Service, said his agency is monitoring Canadian wheat and barley shipments into the U.S., and it appears that shipments are getting close to the 1.4-million- to 1.5-million-tonne limit agreed to in a 1994 pact.
"We understand they (Canada) have told us they would try not to exceed this amount (1.4 million to 1.5 million tonnes)," Schumacher said.
Schumacher said officials are trying to clarify these reports, and that grain consultations with the Canadians are scheduled for next week.
Schumacher repeated warnings from U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky, and said, "This administration simply will not tolerate market disruptions by Canadian grain."

"The United States will not sit idly by and permit another surge in imports, such as that which occurred in 1994. The United States is not going to be the dumping ground for Canada's large grain supplies," said Schumacher.
He also said that with regard to Canadian Wheat Board, USDA has seen little progress to date in implementing the policy recommendations of the U.S.-Canada Joint Commission on Grains.

Schumacher said that despite a NAFTA panel ruling in December upholding Canadian tariffs on U.S. exports of barley, dairy, poultry and egg products, Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman has pledged to do "everything possible to seek the elimination of Canada's exorbitantly high duties."
